 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Athish Tejashwi Kumar, Son of B.M.Thejaswi in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. Facts leading to the case of the petitioners forthcoming in the petition that on 28.04.2024 at about 3.20 p.m. the deceased was riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-KK-3084 proceeding from Dasarahalli towards his home, when he reached near Gangondanahalli bridge, Madavara - Electronic City Nice Road,
Bangalore city, at that time driver of Canter Container Lorry bearing registration No.MH- 46-BF-8947 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and stopped the same in middle of the road without giving any signal or indicator at no parking area.
As a result of which, the deceased motor cycle dashed back side of the canter container lorry and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is stated in the petition that, immediately after the accident, Athish Tejashwi Kumar was shifted to Arkavathi Hospital, Bengaluru for first aid, then he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital and died in the said hospital during the course of treatment.

After completion of Post mortem at St.John's Hospital,
Bengaluru, dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

4. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale, healthy and working as a Software Engineer in (Grade-D2), in Axcend Automation & Software Solutions Private Ltd.,
Bengaluru and was earning Rs.80,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Due to the untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners fell in dark and mental agony.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the canter container lorry bearing registration No.MH-46-BF-8947.

In this regard, jurisdictional police have registered criminal case in Crime No.174/2024 for the offences punishable under section 279, 283 and 304(A)
of I.P.C. As such
, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. In spite of service of the notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, hence, placed exparte.

On the other hand respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel Thejaswi B M vs Lovely Ramgopal Sharma on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33906506/

sentences.text: 7. In the written statement the respondent No.2 has contended that the accident was not occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry alone but also the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-03-KK- 3084.
Further admitted about the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.MH- 46-BF-8947 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle on the date of accident.
It is also contention of the respondent that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the respondent No.2.
8.

On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this court had framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Athish Tejashwi Kumar died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 28.4.2024 at about 3.20 p.m. under Gangondanahalli Bridge, Madavara-Electronic City, Nice Road,
Bengalruru City due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.MH-46-BF-8947 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
4) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 has examined as PW1 got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P30.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of HR at Axcend Automation & Software Solution Pvt. Ltd., by name Nithin Jain M. as PW2 and got marked the documents Ex.P31 to Ex.P41.

Consequently, Athish Tejashwi Kumar had died in the said accident.

ISSUE No.2 & 3;
20.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P26 to Ex.P30 Aadhar cards and Genealogical tree of the petitioners and the deceased, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

21. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioners No.1 and 2 in their middle age, lost their son, as well as the care of their son, and the petitioner No.3 has lost his brother, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners, at the time of cross-examination of the PW1.
By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.

22. The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased, as on the date of the accident,
have placed Driving Licence and Aadhar card marked at Ex.P25 & Ex.P26.

On going through same,
the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 16.06.1995.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
The alleged accident had occurred on 28.4.2024.
Hence, I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 29 years.

For his age,
multiplier '17' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

23. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition, and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as a Software Engineer (Grade D2) in Axcend Automation &
Software Solution Private Limited and was drawing salary of Rs.80,000/- per month.

25. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
26.
Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.

In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor,
deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 29 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "17" is applicable.

And by relying on the principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the petitioner herein as on the date of the accident, deceased Athish Tejashwi Kumar was on job.
On perusal of appointment letter as per Ex.P15, it appears that he was put 6 months for probationary period, thereafter his service had been confirmed.
Therefore, it is held that deceased was having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 50%
income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects as the deceased was below 40 years age.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.6,79,585/- per annum.
Along with this, the future prospects of 50% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.6,79,585+3,39,792)= Rs.10,19,377/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus net loss income comes to Rs.5,09,688.50 (Rs.10,19,377-Rs.5,09,688.50).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "17".
Which comes to Rs.86,64,704/- .
27.

sentences.text: National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

28. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 & 2 under the head loss of consortium.

sentences.text: As per the records insurance policy was valid from 5.4.2024 to 4.4.2025.
The alleged accident had taken place on 28.4.2024.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.4:
34.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.88,42,774/- (Rupees eighty eight lakh forty two thousand seven hundred and seventy four only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 60%, the petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled the share of 20% each.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 to 3, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/- each.
Draw award accordingly.

owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
As per the records insurance policy was valid from 5.4.2024 to 4.4.2025.
The alleged accident had taken place on 28.4.2024.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
